title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
problem: The input has four lines: a whole number N, then N integers in increasing order, then a whole number M, then M integers in increasing order. N can be 0, and then its line of numbers is empty. Print all N + M numbers merged into one increasing list, separated by spaces, keeping repeats. For example, 1 4 7 and 2 4 9 merge into 1 2 4 4 7 9.
starter_code:
# Line 1: N. Line 2: N sorted integers (empty if N is 0).
# Line 3: M. Line 4: M sorted integers.
# Print all the numbers merged into one sorted list, keeping repeats.

# Write your code here

hints.1: Both lists are already in order. Think about repeatedly taking the smaller of the two front numbers.
hints.2: Keep one position in each list. While both have numbers left, append the smaller front number and move that position on; then add whatever is left of the other list. Compare as integers, keep repeats, and remember that an empty line gives an empty list.
hints.3:
input()
a = list(map(int, input().split()))
input()
b = list(map(int, input().split()))
out, i, j = [], 0, 0
while i < len(a) and j < len(b):
    if a[i] <= b[j]:
        out.append(a[i])
        i += 1
    else:
        out.append(b[j])
        j += 1
out += a[i:] + b[j:]
print(' '.join(map(str, out)))

failure_explanation: Keep every number, including repeats, and compare them as integers: sorted as text, a longer number can land before a shorter one that starts with a bigger digit. A list can be empty, so reading its line must give an empty list rather than crash, and the leftover numbers of the longer list go at the end.
